text: Today we're going to discuss database transactions.
A transaction consists of a sequence of operations.
If any operation fails, the entire transaction is rolled back.
Databases also guarantee isolation between concurrent transactions.
This prevents dirty reads and phantom reads.
The locking mechanism ensures that one transaction cannot modify a row another is reading.
We call this a shared lock versus an exclusive lock.
Deadlocks can occur when two transactions wait for each other.
The database detects the deadlock and rolls back one transaction.
